prerequisites.name: Bare-metal lifecycle management
prerequisites.definition: Managing physical servers from racking through provisioning, operation and cleanup for reuse.
prerequisites.why: NICo exists to automate bare-metal lifecycle management.

prerequisites.name: Zero-trust host model
prerequisites.definition: The principle that host OS software is never trusted, so enforcement happens on the DPU and monitoring happens out-of-band.
prerequisites.why: NICo's design is built around zero-trust management of hosts.

prerequisites.name: BlueField DPU
prerequisites.definition: An NVIDIA SmartNIC with its own ARM CPU, OS and BMC, used as NICo's trust anchor.
prerequisites.why: Provisioning DPUs and enforcing isolation through them is a core NICo function.

prerequisites.name: Server hardware basics
prerequisites.definition: How a physical server is built: CPU, memory, drives, NICs and firmware, and how servers sit in datacenter racks.
prerequisites.why: You need to know what a physical server is before you can manage its lifecycle.

prerequisites.name: Multi-tenancy
prerequisites.definition: Several customers sharing the same physical infrastructure while staying isolated from each other.
prerequisites.why: The goal of making machines behave like cloud instances assumes they are shared and reused across tenants.
